You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

steps.input: entry = await rlm.harness.create_memory(title="ARC connect two colored markers with diagonal then straight 3s", content="For sparse ARC grids with two isolated markers (color 1 and color 2) on 0 background, connect them with color 3 by drawing an orthogonal/diagonal polyline that ends diagonally adjacent to marker 2. From marker 1 toward marker 2, advance diagonally in both coordinate directions until the shorter coordinate separation is reduced to 1; then continue along the remaining longer axis until both coordinates are one cell short of marker 2 (thus the endpoint is its diagonal neighbor). Include every path cell after marker 1 through that endpoint; preserve both markers. Example demo: 1 at (r10,c1), 2 at (r3,c11): 3s on (r9,c2)..(r4,c7), then (r4,c8)..(r4,c10). Test: 1 (r1,c4), 2 (r13,c12): diagonal (r2,c5)..(r8,c11), then vertical (r9..r12,c11). Coordinates are zero-based. Equivalent construction: let target-marker coordinate differences have signs sr,sc and magnitudes dr,dc; take min(dr,dc)-1 diagonal steps, then continue on the axis with larger difference until arriving at (target_r-sr,target_c-sc). This is grounded in one demo, so verify orientation/endpoint against any additional demos if available.", path="arc", global_=True); entry
